record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Let G be an abelian-by-nilpotent ordered group. (i) Is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group? (ii) If G is also nilpotent-by-abelian, is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group?

evidence.quote: 3.32∗ . (V. V. Bludov) Let G be an abelian-by-nilpotent ordered group. (i) Is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group? (ii) If G is also nilpotent-by-abelian, is G order-embeddable in a divisible ordered group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A totally ordered group is a group $G$ equipped with a total order $\leq$ that is invariant under both left and right multiplication: for all $a,b,x,y \in G$, $a \leq b$ implies $xay \leq xby$. A totally ordered group $D$ is called divisible if for every $d \in D$ and every positive integer $n$ there exists $x \in D$ with $x^n = d$. An order-embedding of an ordered group $G$ into an ordered group $H$ is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi : G \to H$ such that for all $a,b \in G$, $a \leq b$ if and only if $\varphi(a) \leq \varphi(b)$. A group $G$ is abelian-by-nilpotent if it has a normal abelian subgroup $A \trianglelefteq G$ such that $G/A$ is nilpotent; it is nilpotent-by-abelian if it has a normal nilpotent subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ such that $G/N$ is abelian.

(i) Let $G$ be an abelian-by-nilpotent totally ordered group. Is $G$ order-embeddable in a divisible totally ordered group?

(ii) If, in addition, $G$ is nilpotent-by-abelian, is $G$ order-embeddable in a divisible totally ordered group?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by V. V. Bludov in a list of unsolved problems in ordered and orderable groups (marked with an asterisk indicating open). Searches reveal related results (e.g., Bludov–Medvedev showing every metabelian ordered group has a metabelian orderable divisible extension) but no published resolution of the abelian-by-nilpotent case in either part (i) or (ii). The problem appears to remain open.
